If you thought solar was going to hurt utilities, get a load of solar+storage

I've got solar and am contemplating storage but the payback period is long at the moment. What I've done is out timers on everything so it is off overnight when I have to buy power and we do the energy hungry tasks like washing and drying clothes during the day when we're making our own power. This means while we typically use 16kWh a day, we generate 17kWh on average so we're generating more than we use and we only buy back about 2kWh from the grid. Using storage to keep that much would be possible but the batteries are expensive for now. Another option is to use my Leaf as a battery since it had a lot of storage and we even have a fast charge station down the road so in theory I could go and buy more power if the solar wasn't generating enough to keep us going and go completely off grid. The utilities are driving us this way because they do charge a lot versus what they pay us for our power and they also charge a flat rate for the connection. Using the car would be the most cost effective method at least until home batteries become more affordable.
